answer: Give every identity a network-neighbourhood check: three beacons send unpredictable pulse probes, and the agent must answer within a tight window, proving its routing path and rough region. Probes are logged as a bridge record, so a farm running dozens of fakes from one server room produces identical pulse signatures and collapses into one grove. Only one identity per grove earns paid work; the rest stay unpaid until they prove a separate neighbourhood. Honest agents pass once, while a farmer must rent separate infrastructure per fake, turning cheap copies into full-price deployments.
